summary: A small TypeScript library (resilience-kit, zero runtime dependencies, Node 20.3+) that wraps ANY async call -- an SMS or payment API, another service -- with resilience policies. Everything wraps one shape, Operation<T> = (signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<T>, so a timeout, an open breaker or a client that went away really stops the work, and the core imports no framework. Stage 1: TimeoutPolicy aborts the operation's signal with a TimeoutError AND rejects at once even if the operation ignores its signal (timer and caller listener always removed); RetryPolicy with exponential backoff (100 ms, x2, max 10 s) and full / equal / no jitter, shouldRetry, Retry-After honoured when longer than the backoff (longer than maxRetryAfterMs, default 60 s, gives up), a total deadlineMs, a cancellable backoff wait, no retry after the caller aborted, and the last error rethrown unchanged; RetryBudget = gRPC retry throttling (10 tokens, -1 per failed attempt, +0.1 per success, retry only above half, counted in thousandths); parseRetryAfter, HttpError and isRetryableHttp (network errors, timeouts, 408, 429, 5xx except 501; never a breaker or bulkhead rejection). Simulated retry storm, 1000 calls x 3 attempts to a dead dependency: 3000 attempts without a budget, 1003 with RetryBudget(); over real sockets 20 calls to a closed port made 23 attempts. Stage 2: CircuitBreaker with a count-based sliding window (ring buffer, windowSize 20, minimumCalls 10, threshold 0.5), open -> half-open checked lazily on the next call (no timer), halfOpenMaxCalls probes, errors that are not failures counted as successes, aborted calls not recorded, and GENERATIONS so a slow result from an earlier state cannot push the open timer back, count as a probe or reopen it; Bulkhead with maxConcurrent, a bounded FIFO queue, cancellable waiting and a DIRECT hand-off of the slot to the oldest waiter (no barging). Stage 3: wrap(retry, breaker, bulkhead, timeout) as plain composition with the recommended order backed by four placement experiments in test/wrap.test.ts (each also showing what the wrong order does); one ResilienceEvent stream for all policies (a throwing handler is ignored); an Express adapter (requestSignal aborted on the response's close, resilienceErrorHandler mapping open breaker / full bulkhead to 503 + Retry-After and timeout to 504 with generic bodies, loadShedding) and a NestJS adapter (@RequestSignal(), ResilienceExceptionFilter), tested against a real Express 4.21.2 app and a real NestJS 10.4.15 app; the Express test found that a `status` field on HttpError leaked a dependency's 404 / 401 to OUR client through Express's default handler, so it was renamed upstreamStatus. Found while writing this interview bank and fixed, each with a test and a mutation (F1-F5): policies no longer add abort listeners to the shared never-aborting NEVER signal (50 concurrent calls, no MaxListenersExceededWarning); throwing onRetry / onGiveUp are contained; a throwing isFailure counts as a failure (no stuck half-open); an Infinity Retry-After gives up (retry-after-too-long), only NaN is ignored; a queued caller aborted right after the hand-off does not run. Tests hardened for a busy machine (20 s vitest timeouts, a separate long-timeout route for the disconnect tests, wider real-time margins). 179 tests pass (Windows, Node 20), including a real loopback HTTP server. Mutation checks: stage 1 32 breaks all caught (against 86 tests); stage 2 27 new breaks, 26 caught at first, the survivor K7 (abort listener left on hand-off) closed with a new test; stage 3 22 new breaks all caught at their first run; after the F1-F5 fixes everything was re-run on the final code against the final 179 tests: 86 breaks, all caught; a lowercase drive path made vitest load modules twice and inflated counts, so the trusted numbers come from H:\ runs. Overhead vs cockatiel 3.2.1 (no-op operation, 100 000 calls per round after 20 000 warm-up, median of 5 rounds, Windows 11, AMD Ryzen 5 4500, Node 20.20.1, two runs, ns per call, ours / cockatiel): timeout 7745 and 8194 / 30413 and 31551; retry 361 and 353 / 382 and 411; breaker 229 and 247 / 350 and 370; bulkhead 229 and 271 / 249 and 252; all four wrapped 11356 and 12075 / 35251 and 37269; bare call 146 and 131. Not implemented: a time-based breaker window or slow-call rate, any state shared between processes (each replica has its own budget, breaker and bulkhead), hedged requests, adaptive concurrency, fallbacks, caching, overhead measured under concurrency or on Linux, Fastify / Express 5 / Koa / Hono adapters or tests, npm publishing.

pitch.intro_30s: Maine ek resilience library khud banayi hai, TypeScript mein, bina runtime dependency -- kisi bhi async call ko timeout, backoff aur jitter wale retries, retry budget, circuit breaker aur bulkhead se wrap karti hai. Core framework-free hai, sab AbortSignal par chalta hai, aur Express aur NestJS adapters real apps ke against tested hain. 179 tests, 86 mutation checks sab caught, aur overhead cockatiel ke against measure kiya.
pitch.explain_2min:
Har backend kuch aisa call karta hai jo uske control mein nahi: SMS API, payment gateway, doosri team ki service. Yeh calls fail hoti hain, hang hoti hain, slow hoti hain, aur naive fixes situation aur bigaadte hain -- timeout nahi toh requests pile up, bina backoff retry toh down service par retry storm. cockatiel aur opossum jaisi libraries hain; maine yeh samajhne ke liye khud banayi ki har policy kahan fail hoti hai.

Sab kuch ek shape wrap karta hai: Operation = (signal: AbortSignal) => Promise, bilkul fetch(url, { signal }) jaisa. Isliye TimeoutPolicy sirf wait karna band nahi karti, signal abort karti hai -- test mein server ko connection close dikhta hai.

Stage 1: timeout, retry with exponential backoff aur full jitter default, Retry-After header, total deadline, aur gRPC jaisa RetryBudget. Simulation mein 1000 calls ek dead dependency par: bina budget 3000 attempts, budget ke saath 1003. Retry give up karke LAST error unchanged rethrow karta hai, wrapper nahi.

Stage 2: circuit breaker -- count-based sliding window, lazy half-open, aur generations taaki purane state ka slow result breaker ko galat move na kare. Bulkhead -- FIFO queue aur slot seedha agle waiter ko hand-off, taaki newcomer line na tode.

Stage 3: wrap(retry, breaker, bulkhead, timeout) -- yeh order maine tests se prove kiya, har wrong placement bhi test mein dikhaya. Ek event stream saari policies ke liye. Express aur NestJS adapters: client disconnect par signal abort, open breaker 503 + Retry-After, timeout 504. Express test ne ek real bug pakda: HttpError ka `status` field Express ke default handler se dependency ka 401 hamare client ko bhej deta tha; rename karke upstreamStatus kiya.

Interview bank likhte waqt paanch real bugs mile (jaise shared signal par MaxListenersExceededWarning, throwing isFailure se atka half-open) -- sab fixed, har ek ka test.

Numbers: 179 tests, final run mein 86 mutation checks sab caught, aur cockatiel 3.2.1 ke against per-call overhead do runs mein -- timeout humara lagbhag 4x sasta tha, bulkhead tie. Shared state across replicas aur npm publish nahi kiya.
pitch.deep_5min:
Ek outgoing call ki poori journey, Express route se fetch tak aur wapas.

Setup. Module level par ek baar banta hai: sms = wrap(RetryPolicy, CircuitBreaker, Bulkhead, TimeoutPolicy) -- ek set per dependency, har call share karti hai, warna breaker aur budget kuch seekh hi nahi paate. wrap(a, b, c) ka matlab a(b(c(op))): outermost pehle.

Route. app.post('/notify') mein requestSignal(req, res) ek AbortSignal deta hai. Yeh RESPONSE ke 'close' par sunta hai, request ke nahi, kyunki Node 16 se request body padhte hi 'close' emit karti hai, jo disconnect nahi hai. Aur close par tabhi abort jab res.writableFinished false ho. Signal WeakMap mein cache hota hai, ek response ka ek signal.

Retry. sms.execute(op, signal) pehle RetryPolicy mein. throwIfAborted, attempt 1, aur andar ki layer ko caller ka signal.

Breaker. CircuitBreaker.execute refresh() karta hai: open hai aur openMs beet gaya toh yahin half-open -- koi timer nahi. Closed hai toh current generation note karta hai aur aage jaane deta hai.

Bulkhead. active < maxConcurrent toh slot le lo; warna queue mein jagah hai toh wait (abort listener ke saath); warna BulkheadRejectedError bina operation chalaye.

Timeout. Naya AbortController, caller ke signal se linked, aur setTimeout. Operation ko yeh naya signal milta hai, aur Promise.race operation aur 'signal aborted' ke beech. fetch(url, { signal: s }) chalta hai; !res.ok par HttpError(res.status, parseRetryAfter(header)) -- field upstreamStatus.

Wapas aate hue. Timeout finally mein timer clear karta hai aur caller ke signal se listener hata deta hai. Bulkhead release: queue mein koi hai toh slot seedha usko, active kam hi nahi hota. Breaker record(generation, outcome): isFailure (isRetryableHttp) false hai, jaise 404, toh woh success count hota hai. Window mein minimumCalls ho gaye aur failure rate threshold par pahunchi toh open. Retry: shouldRetry false toh turant give up, budget ko haath nahi. Retryable hai toh budget.onFailure, attempts khatam? budget canRetry? phir backoff delay, Retry-After lamba hai toh woh, deadline check, 'retry' event, aur sleep(delay, signal).

Client disconnect beech mein. Response 'close' -> controller.abort(ClientClosedError). Timeout ka listener apna controller usi reason se abort karta hai, fetch cancel, upstream ko close dikhta hai (Express test isko check karta hai). Bulkhead slot free. Breaker signal.aborted dekh ke outcome 'ignored' -- dependency ki galti nahi thi. Retry signal.aborted dekh ke caller ka reason throw karta hai: na retry, na budget charge. Agar call backoff sleep mein thi toh sleep turant reject; queue mein thi toh waiter queue se nikal jaata hai.

Open breaker. Agli call par breaker 'breaker-rejected' emit karke BrokenCircuitError('open', retryAfterMs) throw karta hai -- operation call nahi hota, bulkhead slot bhi nahi lagta. Retry mein isRetryableHttp is error ko false bolta hai, toh 0 retries, reason not-retryable. Route next(e) karta hai, resilienceErrorHandler 503 bhejta hai, Retry-After = max(1, ceil(ms/1000)) seconds, aur body generic: dependency ka error text kabhi client tak nahi jaata.

Sabse mushkil decisions. Pehla, order: retry outermost taaki breaker har attempt dekhe (har failed attempt record hota hai, 10th -- 4th call ke dauraan -- breaker open karta hai; ulta karo toh 4 outcomes, closed rehta hai), bulkhead retry ke andar taaki backoff sleep slot na pakde, timeout innermost taaki har attempt ki apni deadline ho. Maine order enforce nahi kiya, recommend kiya, lekin har claim ek test hai. Doosra, generations: bina iske closed state mein shuru hui slow failure open hone ke baad aaye toh open timer peeche khisak jaata, ya half-open mein aayi slow success bina asli probe ke breaker band kar deti. Teesra, bulkhead ka direct hand-off: release karke waiter ko jaagne par slot lene do toh beech mein newcomer ghus jaata. Chautha, retry last error unchanged rethrow karta hai, taaki caller ka existing 'instanceof HttpError' wala code chalta rahe. Paanchwa, yeh sab ek process ki memory mein hai -- teen replicas teen breakers; shared state build nahi kiya.
pitch.architecture_walkthrough: src/types.ts: Operation<T> = (signal) => Promise<T> aur Policy interface (execute(operation, signal?)) -- poori library ka ek contract; plus ek shared NEVER signal aur listenable() taaki koi policy us par listener na lagaye. src/errors.ts: TimeoutError (abort reason bhi), BrokenCircuitError (state, retryAfterMs), BulkheadRejectedError, ClientClosedError. src/sleep.ts: cancellable sleep, abort par timer clear. src/timeout.ts: TimeoutPolicy -- apna AbortController, caller signal linked, setTimeout jo 'timeout' event emit karke TimeoutError se abort karta hai, Promise.race, finally mein clearTimeout aur listener remove. src/backoff.ts: exponentialBackoff -- min(maxMs, initialMs x multiplier^(n-1)), jitter none / full / equal, Math.min overflow se bachata hai. src/budget.ts: RetryBudget -- SCALE 1000 integer tokens, canRetry tokens > max/2, onSuccess +ratio capped, onFailure -1 floor 0. src/retry.ts: RetryPolicy -- attempt loop, caller abort check, shouldRetry, budget, maxAttempts, Retry-After aur maxRetryAfterMs, deadlineMs, onRetry / onGiveUp (quietly, throw contained) aur events, test hooks random / sleep / now. src/http.ts: parseRetryAfter (seconds ya HTTP-date), HttpError (upstreamStatus, retryAfterMs), isRetryableHttp. src/breaker.ts: CircuitBreaker -- ring buffer window, minimumCalls, lazy refresh(), probesInFlight / probeSuccesses, generation counter, classify() jo throwing isFailure ko failure ginta hai, transition() jo onStateChange errors swallow karta hai. src/bulkhead.ts: Bulkhead -- active count, Waiter queue, waitForSlot with abort listener, release() jo slot seedha waiter ko deta hai, aur jaagne par abort re-check; running aur queued getters. src/wrap.ts: wrap -- policies ko andar se bahar compose karta hai, har layer ka apna signal aage. src/events.ts: ResilienceEvent union (timeout, retry, give-up, breaker-state, breaker-rejected, bulkhead-rejected) aur emit jo throwing handler ignore karta hai. src/adapters/http-status.ts: mapResilienceError -- 503 + Retry-After, 503 overloaded, 504, generic bodies. src/adapters/express.ts: requestSignal (WeakMap, response 'close'), resilienceErrorHandler, loadShedding. src/adapters/nestjs.ts: @RequestSignal() param decorator aur ResilienceExceptionFilter. src/index.ts: core entry; express aur nestjs alag entry points (package.json exports). test/: 11 test files plus support.ts (loopback upstream server helpers), 179 tests; vitest.config.ts 20 s timeouts (busy machine). bench/overhead.mjs: cockatiel ke against per-call cost, results bench/reference-results/ mein.
difficult_decisions: Core ka contract (signal: AbortSignal) => Promise rakha, framework ka koi type nahi. Yahi fetch aur modern drivers ka shape hai, toh timeout ya disconnect asli kaam rokta hai; adapters alag entry points hain (resilience-kit/express, resilience-kit/nestjs), core unhe import nahi karta, aur Express adapter Express ko bhi import nahi karta, sirf Node ke http types.

Timeout signal ABORT karta hai, sirf promise reject nahi. Sirf waiting band karne wala timeout socket khula aur query chalti chhod deta hai; http.test.ts mein hanging server ko connection close dikhta hai. Saath mein race bhi hai, taaki signal ignore karne wala operation bhi caller ko atka na sake.

Retry give up karke LAST error unchanged rethrow karta hai, RetriesExhaustedError jaisa wrapper nahi -- caller ka existing error handling chalta rahe; attempts aur reason onGiveUp / give-up event mein. Non-retryable error (404) budget ko touch nahi karta, kyunki woh dependency ki health ke baare mein kuch nahi batata.

Breaker mein generations: har state change counter badhata hai, aur call apna outcome sirf usi generation mein record karti hai jismein shuru hui. Teen stale cases ke teen tests hain, aur mutation B9 inhe pakadta hai. Saath mein: non-failures (isFailure false) success count hote hain, ignore nahi, warna 404 dene wali healthy service par kuch 5xx akele faisla kar lete.

Bulkhead slot release nahi karta, seedha oldest waiter ko hand-off karta hai; active count beech mein girta hi nahi, toh newcomer line nahi tod sakta. Release-then-retake simple dikhta hai lekin unfair hai (mutation K4).

Order enforce nahi kiya, recommend kiya (retry -> breaker -> bulkhead -> timeout), aur har placement claim wrap.test.ts mein ek experiment hai jo wrong order ka nateeja bhi dikhata hai -- taaki recommendation evidence ho, folklore nahi.
biggest_challenges: Duplicate-module instanceof artefact: stage 2 ke pehle mutation run mein counts unstable the (same break kabhi 1 test fail, kabhi 6). Extra failures sab 'expected BulkheadRejectedError to be an instance of BulkheadRejectedError' padhte the -- error classes DO BAAR load hui thi kyunki runner ne vitest lowercase drive path (h:\...) se chalaya tha. H:\ se wahi breaks 3 mein se 3 runs mein same counts dete hain, aur clean suite kabhi fail nahi hua (8 of 8). Isi finding ke baad B1 parking lot ka stage 3 mutation run H:\ se dobara chalaya: har break ab bhi caught, lekin 13 counts inflated the. Lesson: noisy mutation count kisi break ko caught dikha sakta hai jab woh caught na ho -- unexpected failures ko naam se check karo.

HttpError status leak: pehle HttpError ka field `status` tha. Express ka default error handler err.status client ko bhejta hai, toh real Express app ke test mein dependency ka 404 hamara 404 ban gaya, aur 401 hamare client ko bolta ki WOH unauthorized hai. Stage 3 mein upstreamStatus rename kiya; ab upstream error plain 500 banta hai jab tak app khud map na kare. Mutation H1 (field wapas status) 3 tests mein pakda jaata hai.

Budget test jo retry expect karta tha: recovery test mein maine socha 51 successes ke baad canRetry() true hai toh agla blip retry hoga. Nahi hua: failing attempt check se PEHLE token deta hai (5.1 - 1 = 4.1, half se neeche). Code sahi tha, expectation galat thi; ab test yeh behaviour state karta hai aur 72 successes total ke baad hi single failure retry hota hai.

No-barging test jo pehle barging test hi nahi karta tha: direct hand-off ko prove karne ke liye newcomer ko EXACTLY us gap mein aana chahiye -- release ke turant baad aur waiter ke continuation se pehle. Pehle version mein newcomer us gap mein nahi aata tha, toh release-then-retake wala bug bhi pass ho jaata. Ab test newcomer ko c.promise('a').then(...) se schedule karta hai, jo bulkhead ke release ke turant baad chalta hai, aur K4 isse pakda jaata hai.

Stage 2 ka survivor K7: waiter ko slot milne par uska abort listener caller ke signal par reh jaata tha -- leak, lekin koi visible effect nahi, isliye koi test fail nahi hua. Ek test add kiya jo signal ke addEventListener / removeEventListener ko spy karta hai; K7 ab caught hai.
failure_scenarios: Dependency hang ho jaaye: har attempt TimeoutPolicy (example mein 2000 ms) par abort, fetch cancel, retry agla attempt; sab fail toh TimeoutError, adapter 504 deta hai. Bulkhead ki wajah se hanging dependency sirf apne slots pakad sakti hai -- http.test.ts mein 6 calls, 2 server tak pahunchi aur timeout hui, 4 turant refuse.

Dependency poori down: breaker window bharne par open, phir openMs tak har call BrokenCircuitError bina network ke (test mein 20 calls, server ko 0 requests); retry isRetryableHttp se turant ruk jaata hai; client ko 503 + Retry-After. Retry budget bhi drain hota hai: 1000 calls par 3000 ki jagah 1003 attempts.

Server 429 ke saath 'Retry-After: 3600' bole: backoff se lamba hai, lekin maxRetryAfterMs (60 s default) se bhi lamba, toh retry wait nahi karta, reason 'retry-after-too-long' ke saath give up -- request park nahi hoti.

Half-open probe kabhi khatam na ho: probe slot hamesha ke liye bhara rehta hai aur breaker half-open mein atka rehta hai. Isiliye TimeoutPolicy breaker ke ANDAR honi chahiye; library isko enforce nahi karti (wrap.test.ts mein dono cases ka test hai).

Operation apna signal ignore kare (jaise purana driver): TimeoutPolicy phir bhi time par reject karti hai aur caller free ho jaata hai, lekin kaam background mein chalta rehta hai -- socket ya query band nahi hoti. Library yeh rok nahi sakti; signal pass karna caller ki zimmedari hai.

Teen API replicas aur dependency down: har replica ka apna breaker, budget aur bulkhead hai, toh har replica alag se seekhta hai ki dependency down hai, aur total load 3 guna hota hai. Shared state (jaise Redis) build nahi kiya.
improvements: Shared state across replicas: breaker state aur retry budget ko Redis jaise store mein rakhna, taaki ek replica ka seekha baaki ko bhi pata ho. Abhi sab ek process ki memory mein hai; latency aur store ke down hone ka trade-off sochna padega. Build nahi kiya.

Breaker mein time-based window aur slow-call rate: abhi window count-based hai (last N calls), toh kam traffic par purane outcomes reh sakte hain, aur slow calls tabhi failure hain jab andar TimeoutPolicy ho. resilience4j ki tarah time buckets aur slow-call threshold add karna.

Adapters ka coverage: NestJS sirf platform-express par tested hai, Fastify par nahi; Express 5 ka test nahi chala (Node http types ke against likha hai, lekin run nahi kiya); Koa / Hono ke adapters nahi hain.

npm par publish karna: abhi package private hai, repo se copy ya local path dependency se use hota hai. Publish ke liye versioning, changelog aur CI chahiye. Saath mein test-only dev dependency @nestjs/platform-express 10.x multer 1.x laata hai jise npm deprecated aur vulnerable bolta hai -- ship nahi hota, lekin upgrade karna chahiye.
Hedged requests, adaptive concurrency limits, fallbacks aur caching: tail latency aur overload ke liye agle policies; abhi koi bhi implement nahi hai.

Overhead ka better measurement: abhi ek Windows PC, do runs, sequential calls. Concurrency ke under aur Linux par measure karna, aur yeh investigate karna ki cockatiel ka timeout kyun mehenga hai -- woh investigate nahi kiya.

steps: 1. Concept: AbortController / AbortSignal -- ek cancel token jo fetch aur drivers samajhte hain. Promise.race sirf WAIT karna band karta hai; signal abort karne se kaam khud rukta hai.
2. Project need: hanging SMS ya payment call request ko pakde rakhti hai, socket khula rehta hai; aur jo client chala gaya uske liye kaam karte rehna waste hai.
3. Code/API: types.ts mein Operation<T> = (signal) => Promise<T>; timeout.ts TimeoutPolicy({ ms }).execute(op, callerSignal); sleep.ts cancellable sleep.

4. Detail: naya AbortController, caller ka abort usse linked; timer TimeoutError se abort karta hai aur 'timeout' event emit; stopped promise kisi bhi abort par reject; async wrapper sync throw ko rejection banata hai; finally mein clearTimeout aur removeEventListener (no leak).
5. Demo: cd projects/18-resilience && npx vitest run test/timeout.test.ts, aur npx vitest run test/http.test.ts -t 'server that hangs' -- TimeoutError aur server ko connection close dikhta hai.
6. Interviewer next: operation signal ignore kare toh kya hota hai, aur database query ko kaise cancel karoge?

learning_path.concept: Retry with exponential backoff and jitter
steps: 1. Concept: transient failure par dobara try, har baar lamba wait (exponential), aur jitter taaki saath fail hue clients saath wapas na aayein (thundering herd).
2. Project need: network blips aur 503 normal hain; lekin bina backoff ke retry down service ko aur dabaata hai.
3. Code/API: backoff.ts exponentialBackoff({ initialMs: 100, multiplier: 2, maxMs: 10000, jitter: 'full' }); retry.ts RetryPolicy({ maxAttempts: 3, backoff, shouldRetry }).

4. Detail: ceiling = min(maxMs, initialMs x multiplier^(n-1)) -- Math.min overflow se bachata hai; full = random [0, value), equal = value/2 + random [0, value/2), none = exact. Give up par last error unchanged; caller abort ke baad kabhi retry nahi; backoff wait bhi cancellable.
5. Demo: cd projects/18-resilience && npx vitest run test/backoff.test.ts test/retry.test.ts -- 'fail, fail, succeed: 3 calls, waits 100 and 200, an event per retry'.
6. Interviewer next: full jitter vs equal jitter kab, aur non-idempotent POST ko retry karna kab galat hai?

learning_path.concept: Retry-After, deadlines and which errors to retry
steps: 1. Concept: har error retry ke laayak nahi -- 4xx wahi request dobara wahi jawab degi; server khud bata sakta hai kab aana hai (Retry-After); aur poore call ka ek total time budget hota hai.
2. Project need: 404 ya 401 retry karna sirf load badhata hai; 429 par jaldi aana sirf ek aur 429 laata hai; user ki request ka total time bounded chahiye.
3. Code/API: http.ts parseRetryAfter(header), HttpError(upstreamStatus, retryAfterMs), isRetryableHttp; RetryPolicy options retryAfterMs, maxRetryAfterMs (60 s), deadlineMs.

4. Detail: retryable = non-HTTP errors, 408, 429, 5xx except 501; BrokenCircuitError aur BulkheadRejectedError kabhi nahi. Retry-After sirf tab jab backoff se lamba ho; maxRetryAfterMs se lamba toh give up 'retry-after-too-long'; jo retry deadline ke baad SHURU hota woh nahi hota ('deadline').
5. Demo: cd projects/18-resilience && npx vitest run test/http.test.ts -t 'Retry-After' -- 429 + 'Retry-After: 1' par policy 1000 ms wait karti hai; aur -t '404 is not retried'.
6. Interviewer next: HTTP-date wala Retry-After clock skew ke saath kaise handle hoga?
1. Concept: retry storm -- 3 attempts per call matlab down dependency ko 3x traffic, layers ke saath 27x. Retry budget (gRPC retry throttling) success rate ke hisaab se retries band kar deta hai.
2. Project need: outage mein retries khud band hon aur recovery par khud wapas aayein, bina manual switch ke.
3. Code/API: budget.ts RetryBudget({ maxTokens: 10, tokenRatio: 0.1 }) -- onFailure, onSuccess, canRetry, available; RetryPolicy({ budget }) shared per dependency.

4. Detail: tokens thousandths mein (SCALE 1000), toh 50 x 0.1 exactly 5; retry sirf tokens > max/2; failing attempt check se PEHLE pay karta hai, toh canRetry true hone ke turant baad bhi ek single failure retry nahi hota. Non-retryable errors budget nahi chhoote.

5. Demo: cd projects/18-resilience && npx vitest run test/budget.test.ts -- 1000 calls: bina budget 3000 attempts, budget ke saath 1003; recovery: 51 successes par canRetry true, 72 total par blip retry. Real sockets: npx vitest run test/http.test.ts -t 'connection refused' (20 calls, 23 attempts).
6. Interviewer next: budget aur circuit breaker dono kyun -- kya ek kaafi nahi?

learning_path.concept: Circuit breaker: sliding window, lazy half-open, generations
steps: 1. Concept: closed -> open (failure rate threshold par) -> half-open (openMs ke baad probe) -> closed ya wapas open. Open mein call network tak jaati hi nahi.
2. Project need: down dependency ko rest dena aur apne callers ko timeout ka wait karane ke bajaye turant fail karna.

3. Code/API: breaker.ts CircuitBreaker({ failureRateThreshold: 0.5, windowSize: 20, minimumCalls: 10, openMs: 30000, halfOpenMaxCalls: 1, isFailure }); state, failureRate; BrokenCircuitError(state, retryAfterMs).

4. Detail: ring buffer window; minimumCalls se pehle koi faisla nahi; refresh() next call par half-open karta hai (koi timer nahi); probe slot reuse nahi hota; isFailure false = success; aborted call record nahi; generation counter stale results ko ignore karta hai; close par window empty.

5. Demo: cd projects/18-resilience && npx vitest run test/breaker.test.ts -t 'generations' (3 stale cases), aur npx vitest run test/http.test.ts -t 'circuit breaker' -- open hone ke baad 20 calls, server ko 0 requests.
6. Interviewer next: count-based vs time-based window, aur 3 replicas ka breaker state share kaise karoge (yahan built nahi)?

learning_path.concept: Bulkhead: bounded FIFO queue and direct hand-off
steps: 1. Concept: bulkhead (ship ke watertight compartments) -- ek dependency ko max N concurrent calls, baaki bounded queue mein ya turant reject.
2. Project need: ek slow dependency process ke saare sockets / workers na kha jaaye; baaki routes chalte rahein.
3. Code/API: bulkhead.ts Bulkhead({ maxConcurrent, maxQueue: 0 }), running, queued; BulkheadRejectedError; Express mein loadShedding(bulkhead) incoming requests ke liye.

4. Detail: release() queue.shift() karke waiter ko resolve karta hai aur active ko girne nahi deta -- direct hand-off, no barging. Queued waiter ka caller abort kare toh woh queue se nikal ke caller ke reason se reject; slot milne par abort listener remove (K7).

5. Demo: cd projects/18-resilience && npx vitest run test/bulkhead.test.ts -t 'no barging', aur npx vitest run test/http.test.ts -t 'bulkhead' -- 6 calls hanging server par, 2 pahunchti hain, 4 turant refuse.
6. Interviewer next: maxConcurrent kaise choose karoge (Little's law), aur fixed limit ki jagah adaptive concurrency kab?

learning_path.concept: Composition order and one event stream
steps: 1. Concept: policies ek doosre ko wrap karti hain; order behaviour badal deta hai. wrap(a, b, c) = a(b(c(op))).
2. Project need: galat order chupke se protection tod deta hai -- breaker outage miss kare, ya bulkhead sleep karti call ke liye slot pakde.
3. Code/API: wrap.ts wrap(retry, breaker, bulkhead, timeout); events.ts ResilienceEvent union aur emit; har policy ka name aur onEvent.

4. Detail: timeout andar = har attempt ki deadline (bahar ho toh 3rd attempt hota hi nahi); breaker retry ke andar = har failed attempt record, 10th (4th call mein) open karta hai (bahar 4 outcomes, closed); open breaker + isRetryableHttp = 0 retries; bulkhead retry ke andar = backoff mein slot free. Throwing event handler kuch nahi badalta.
5. Demo: cd projects/18-resilience && npx vitest run test/wrap.test.ts -- 'why the recommended order is retry -> breaker -> bulkhead -> timeout' aur exact event sequence wala test.
6. Interviewer next: fallback policy add karni ho toh order mein kahan rakhoge?

learning_path.concept: Framework adapters: request signal, 503/504 mapping, upstreamStatus
steps: 1. Concept: library ko framework se jodna -- client disconnect ko AbortSignal banana, aur resilience errors ko sahi HTTP status mein badalna, bina dependency ki details leak kiye.
2. Project need: owner ke Express aur NestJS projects; disconnect par upstream call band ho, aur client ko 503 / 504 mile, 500 nahi.

3. Code/API: adapters/express.ts requestSignal(req, res), resilienceErrorHandler(), loadShedding(bulkhead); adapters/nestjs.ts @RequestSignal(), ResilienceExceptionFilter; adapters/http-status.ts mapResilienceError.

4. Detail: response ke 'close' par abort (request ka close disconnect nahi), sirf jab writableFinished false; WeakMap cache. Open breaker 503 + Retry-After (kam se kam 1), full bulkhead 503 + Retry-After 1, timeout 504; unknown errors next(). HttpError ka field upstreamStatus kyunki Express ka default handler err.status client ko bhejta tha.

5. Demo: cd projects/18-resilience && npx vitest run test/express.test.ts test/nestjs.test.ts test/http-status.test.ts -- 'an upstream 404 / 401 is NOT passed on' aur 'the client disconnects -> the upstream request is cancelled'.
6. Interviewer next: Fastify ya Express 5 ke liye kya badlega (yahan tested nahi), aur 503 par Retry-After kaise calculate hota hai?

learning_path.concept: Testing a resilience library: hooks, real servers, mutation checks, overhead
steps: 1. Concept: time aur randomness wale code ko deterministic test karna (injected hooks, fake timers), real I/O ke against bhi chalana, aur mutation checks se test suite ki taakat naapna.
2. Project need: retries, timers aur races tabhi trust hote hain jab test exact waits aur interleavings dikhaye; aur 'humari library sasti hai' claim ko number chahiye.

3. Code/API: RetryPolicy ke random / sleep / now hooks; CircuitBreaker ka now; vi.useFakeTimers jahan real timer behaviour point hai; test/support.ts loopback upstream; bench/overhead.mjs cockatiel 3.2.1 ke against.

4. Detail: 179 tests; mutation checks 32 + 27 + 22 breaks + F1-F5, stage 2 ka K7 test add karke closed, final code par 86 sab caught; busy machine par flaky tests (tight real-time margins, 5 s hook timeout) wider margins aur vitest.config.ts 20 s timeouts se theek kiye; lowercase drive path par vitest ne modules do baar load kiye (instanceof fail), isliye trusted runs H:\ se. Bench: 100 000 calls per round, 20 000 warm-up, median of 5 rounds, do runs; timeout 7745 / 8194 ns vs cockatiel 30413 / 31551 -- ek machine, sequential, sirf wrapper cost.
5. Demo: cd projects/18-resilience && npm test (179 tests), npm run bench (results bench/reference-results/ mein), aur README.md ke 'Mutation checks' aur 'Overhead' sections.
6. Interviewer next: mutation count achanak badal jaaye toh kya check karoge, aur micro-benchmark se production ke baare mein kya nahi keh sakte?
